studies.title: The Earth Tells Its News
studies.meaning: The surah opens on a condition and withholds the main clause. When the earth is shaken with its own shaking, and brings out its own burdens. Everything in those two lines is attached to the ground by a possessive, so the quake belongs to it and so does the load. Then a human voice arrives with three words, and it is a question rather than a cry: what is wrong with it. The answer is that the earth will report, and the reason given is that God inspired it to.
studies.historicalContext: The classical sources divide over whether this surah is Meccan or Medinan and record the disagreement without settling it. Either way it belongs with the short chapters that describe the last day as one continuous scene rather than as an argument. Earthquakes were known in the region and needed no explaining. What is new in the passage is the ground having something to say afterwards.

keyTerms.note: A doubled root that imitates repeated motion, with a possessive attached. The shaking is called the earth's own, as though it were something the ground had been holding in and finally does.
A plural of what is heavy, used both of carried loads and of the weight of a pregnancy. It occurs only here in the Quran, and commentators read it of the dead and of whatever else the ground holds.
The verb used for revelation given to prophets, and also for the instruction given to the bee. Applied to the earth it makes the report a communication received rather than a memory being replayed.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: The ground kept everything. People were buried in it, valuables were buried in it for safety when a family travelled, cisterns and wells were cut down into it, and a disputed boundary was argued over the dirt itself. For an audience that hid things in the earth as a matter of routine and trusted it to hold them, a picture of the ground giving up what it carries and then explaining itself was a very particular kind of exposure.
studies.didYouKnow: The plural used for the earth's burdens occurs only once in the Quran. The first five ayat of the surah also all end on the same attached pronoun, so the ground is grammatically the subject of everything until people arrive in the sixth line, where the ending changes. The chapter is about the earth before it is about anyone standing on it.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Testimony is taken from outside the human world, which changes what a record is. Nothing has to be remembered by any person, or written by any clerk, for it to be reported, because the place where an act happened is itself a witness with a channel of communication opened to it. The passage also removes the last private setting: there is no location that is merely scenery.

crossReferences.why: Describes the same moment from the earth's side, casting out what is in it and listening to its Lord.
Has a person's own skin testify against him, and explains that God gave speech to everything.
Uses the same verb of inspiration for the instruction given to the bee, outside any human recipient.

studies.applyIt: Think of a room or a street corner where something happened that you have never told anyone about. Picture the place rather than the event. The surah is not asking you to confess to anybody. It is pointing out that the setting was never neutral, and that is a strange and useful thing to sit with for a minute.

studies.title: An Atom's Weight, Seen
studies.meaning: People come out in scattered groups, and the purpose is stated in the passive: to be shown their works. Not judged yet, shown. Then two lines with identical structure and one word changed, so the sentence about good and the sentence about evil are the same sentence. The unit of measurement is the smallest thing the language had, and the verb at the end is seeing rather than being told.
studies.historicalContext: Medinan by the tradition this collection follows, though the classical authorities differ and many place the surah in Mecca. No set occasion is reported. It closes a chapter of eight short ayat. In them the earth is shaken, gives up its weight, and then speaks. So the shown record arrives after the ground itself has testified.

keyTerms.note: Classically explained as the smallest ant or as the specks of dust visible in a sunbeam. It names the limit of what the eye can register, which is exactly the point of the sentence.
The plural of the word for what is dispersed, the same root used elsewhere of human efforts running in different directions. People arrive sorted rather than in one crowd.

A word from the scales, the standard weight a merchant set against goods. Pairing it with the smallest particle makes the image precise: the balance is set far below anything a person would bother to record.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Merchants carried sets of weights and a balance. The smallest weights were used for gold dust and for perfume, in amounts a customer had to trust the seller about. Disputes over a fraction were common. The image of a scale reading down to a mote spoke straight to people who knew exactly how much cheating happened at the bottom of a set of weights.
studies.didYouKnow: A report in the early collections describes the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) answering a question about the reward for keeping animals. He answered by reciting these two ayat. The wording of the report calls them the singular, all-gathering ayah. Two short lines were treated as enough for a question they do not mention, because the measure they set covers everything.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The symmetry of the two lines is the theology. Good and evil are weighed on the same scale, at the same resolution, with the same verb, so neither is treated as the default and neither is rounded away. That removes two comforts at once: the idea that small good deeds are not worth doing, and the idea that small wrongs do not count. The record is also shown rather than described, which makes the reckoning a matter of recognition.

crossReferences.why: Uses the same unit to describe God's justice, promising that nothing that small is mishandled.
Describes the same completeness from the other side, a book that omits nothing and the dismay of finding it so.
Applies the same smallness to hidden places, promising that a mustard seed is retrievable from anywhere.

studies.applyIt: Do one good thing today that is too small to mention: pick something off the floor, hold a door, send a two-word message. Then deliberately do not tell anyone. The scale in this ayah is set below the level you would normally bother with. So most of your record is being written in a register you are not watching.
studies.explainEasier: On that day people will come out in groups to be shown what they did. Anyone who did even a speck of good will see it. Anyone who did even a speck of harm will see that too.
